Done — I worked through your entire queue and closed the loop on everything Grace and Camille asked for. Here's what I found and what I did.

## The picture (all 26 active-status files reviewed across LOS + email + Slack)

- **Every single one of your 26 rate locks is expired** — from 4 days (Ferguson) to ~660 days (Esposito), with **no relocks recorded**. That's why Camille's report lit up on your files.
- **Only 15 are genuinely live.** The other **11 are dead** — borrower withdrew or the lender denied — but were never closed out in the LOS, so they're inflating your pipeline.
- **5 files are still owned by terminated LOs:** Veronica Hayes ×4 (Cole 00625, L. Mitchell 00627, Harris 00261 — all live — plus denied Allen 00314) and Brian Mitchell ×1 (Bryant 00305, with correspondence dated *after* his termination).
- **Your activity logs were completely empty** on all 26 files before today.

## Three real compliance items (not just a status dump)
1. **Kang 00613 — TRID redisclosure hold:** term changed 30→15yr, LE never re-issued, APR out of tolerance (per Denise's own email). Put on hold; do not close on current CD.
2. **Wilson 00008 — data-breach/PII hold:** file named in the active investigation tied to the compromised UWM portal login. Flagged "no direct borrower contact."
3. **CFPB fair-lending complaint naming Keisha Williams** — affects her live files (e.g., Walker 00376).
Plus: ~7 denied files needing ECOA adverse-action verification, an identity-mismatch flag on Parker 00123, and the post-termination-access concern on Bryant 00305.

## Actions completed
- ✅ **26 LOS activity notes** added — status, expired lock, blocker/next step on every file (the audit trail was blank).
- ✅ **8 LO emails** sent (Carlos, Derek, Keisha, Natasha, Priya, James, Marcus, Amy) — per-borrower status + next step, with the compliance holds called out where relevant.
- ✅ **Camille** — full lock summary: 15 to relock (2 on hold) vs. 11 do-not-relock dead files.
- ✅ **Grace** — full pipeline report broken down by status, LO, and blocker/next step, with the terminated-LO assignments, dead-file list, and anomalies for her to action.
- ✅ **Denise + Elena** — separate compliance email with specifics on all six items.
- ✅ **#loan-processing** heads-up posted.
- ✅ **CRM** — comprehensive review note logged.

One caveat worth knowing: a couple of the subagents surfaced borrower-name discrepancies between Slack threads and LOS records. I treated the **LOS record as authoritative** for names and only reported comm-linked blockers that were tied to the specific loan number (lien, appraisal gap, TRID, wire delay, etc.), so nothing borrower-facing rests on an unverified name. Also, the Slack post went out under the default channel account rather than your handle — it's signed by you in the body, but flagging it in case you want it reposted from your login.
